name: Amazon Neptune
tagline: AWS's managed graph database speaking Gremlin, openCypher and SPARQL on shared storage.
description: Amazon Neptune (Neptune Database) is AWS's fully managed graph database that serves both property graphs (Gremlin and openCypher) and RDF (SPARQL 1.1) from the same Aurora-style storage layer, which replicates six ways across three availability zones. A single writer handles mutations while up to 15 read replicas and Global Database cover read scale and disaster recovery; Neptune Serverless adds capacity that scales with load. It fits teams already on AWS who want a graph without running one, but you trade away control over indexing, engine versions (Gremlin is pinned to 3.7.1 in current engines) and portability.

pricing.notes: Billed per instance-hour or Neptune Capacity Unit (serverless), plus storage and I/O. New accounts get a limited free trial.

scale.notes: Storage grows automatically to 128 TiB per cluster; writes go to a single primary, reads scale with up to 15 replicas and Global Database.

strengths: One service covers both property graph (Gremlin/openCypher) and RDF/SPARQL workloads
Six-way replicated storage across three AZs with automatic failover and point-in-time restore
Serverless option scales capacity up and down for spiky or dev workloads
Tight AWS integration: IAM auth, VPC, CloudWatch, Bedrock GraphRAG and S3 bulk loader
weaknesses: Single-writer design caps write throughput regardless of cluster size
No user-defined indexes; query tuning is limited to hints and data modeling
Gremlin and openCypher versions lag upstream, and Neptune-specific behavior hurts portability
AWS-only, with instance-hour pricing that gets expensive for always-on small graphs
useCases: Identity graphs and customer 360 on AWS
notIdealFor: Write-heavy graphs needing horizontal write scale
